reasoning.result: ABS reports All groups CPI annual movement of 3.8 percent in Dec-25, 3.8 in Jan-26, 3.7 in Feb-26, 4.6 in Mar-26, 4.2 in Apr-26, and 4.0 in May-26.

reasoning.text: The reference class is the recent six-point official headline annual-rate history. The March spike has partly reversed, while the July comparison base includes a large July 2025 monthly increase, creating downside pressure on the annual rate if July 2026 monthly inflation is more normal.

Level, momentum, one-off, and policy mechanisms: the level remains above the recent 3.7 percent trough; momentum has eased from 4.6 to 4.0 percent; the July 2025 base effect is a downside adjustment; housing and services persistence provide an offsetting upside adjustment.

Prior/update/interval: persistence prior is the recent ABS six-point headline annual-rate sample [3.8, 3.8, 3.7, 4.6, 4.2, 4.0], updated downward for the July 2025 base effect and recent easing but partly offset by persistent housing/services inflation. Successive changes are [0.0,-0.1,0.9,-0.4,-0.2], giving sigma = 0.50 percentage points; the 80% half-width is roughly 1.28*0.50 = 0.64, implying unrounded bounds of about 3.3 to 4.5 after centering at 3.9.

Downside risk is a normal July monthly print replacing the unusually strong July 2025 base, which could put annual inflation below 3.3 percent. Upside risk is renewed transport, housing, or services pressure; a broad reacceleration would land above the interval.
Point estimate 3.9 percent; interval calculation 3.9 - 0.64 = 3.26 and 3.9 + 0.64 = 4.54, rounded to the ABS one-decimal reporting grid as 3.3 to 4.5 percent.
